notes:
### N031.1 — What the course announcement proposes

The page presents “Géométrie de l’icosaèdre” as a proposed common investigation beginning with combinatorial intuition and coloured cardboard models. It announces a detailed dictionary between the oriented combinatorial icosahedron and an oriented five-element set, refers to their common automorphism group as the alternating group on five letters, and proposes geometric realizations over real and other fields, with vector, affine and projective geometry involved. The historical opening is qualified by “ne semble jamais”; the course “se voudrait” an investigation. Those are the author’s formulations, not independently established historical conclusions.

### N031.2 — Mathematics-directed and typographic reading decisions

The handwritten A before the typed low 5 retains the alphabet alternatives frak A / cal A; its mathematical name does not settle the pen’s alphabet. The heading initial has an offset lower/right edge and retains the doubled-letter encoding. In the second paragraph’s first icosaèdre, the faint crossbar and lower return beneath the live c support recovery of deleted e. The root retains the one-cell dash after arètes !) and removes the extra blank between ensemble and the opening quote of orienté. The printed letterhead, its two rules, the distant course-heading rule and the close topic underline are preserved. A detached pair at the right margin and an opaque oblique shape beside archive 30 receive geometric representations without assigned verbal roles.

### N031.3 — Check actually performed

The root enumerated the 60 even permutations of five elements. The conjugacy-class sizes were 1, 20, 15, 12 and 12; closing each nonidentity class with the identity under products produced all 60 elements. Every nontrivial normal subgroup contains one such class and its products, establishing simplicity. The explicit permutations p=(1 2 3) and q=(3 4 5) yielded p∘q=(1 2 3 4 5) and q∘p=(1 2 4 5 3), establishing noncommutativity. This exhaustive computation and its elementary proof interpretation are documented in decisions/scan031_math_checks.md, decisions/scan031_A5_check.json and scripts/check_A5.py. The source’s additional minimal-order claim and the proposed geometric dictionary were not independently proved in this run. No glyph was chosen from the computation.

### N031.4 — Titles, dates and page metadata

The centered heading reads “COURS C4 1977-78 de A. GROTHENDIECK”; the topic heading is singly underlined. The institutional letterhead includes an unfilled “Montpellier, le” field. No day/month dateline is entered. The lower-corner archive number is 30 (scan 31). This is a typescript with the group capital added by hand.
